transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-03-27 16:00 UTC / Duration 52 min / Recording: yes
Attendees: Amira (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Sofia (Redwood Solutions Eng), Jordan (Veridian Eng Lead), Priya (ML Eng), Marco (Security), Leah (Product)
---
00:00 Amira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Amira from Redwood. Quick intros?
00:12 Jordan: Jordan here, eng lead at Veridian, we run the ML infra and operations for our assistant product.
00:18 Priya: Priya, ML engineer, main engineer on the inference stack.
00:22 Marco: Marco, security architect — I'll be looking at compliance and KMS stuff.
00:28 Leah: Leah, product, I'll handle success criteria and timelines.
00:33 Amira: Great — Liam, Sofia on my side?
00:36 Liam: Yep hi, Liam, solutions engineering, I usually run the POCs and perf benches.
00:40 Sofia: Sofia, will help with onboarding + integration patterns.
:45 Amira: High level, we heard you're evaluating portability from OpenAI/Anthropic and some on-prem vLLM work? Can you describe current setup and pain points?
01:02 Jordan: Sure — our stack's a mix. For 70% of user queries we use OpenAI for chat and a handful of Anthropic flows for safety-sensitive prompts. For heavy internal workloads we started self-hosting via vLLM on a fleet of A10s with TGI adapters for some models. The pain: cost unpredictability on hosted vendors, and vLLM ops fragility — bursts kill latency.
01:27 Priya: Also model parity is a problem — responses drift between providers, tokenization differences, sampling params not identical. Our SREs want predictable latency <200ms median for short chat turns.
01:44 Leah: Timeline: we want to pick a direction for Q2 POC and then decide for production in Q3. Security's gating is non-negotiable — SOC2 and KMS integration.
02:00 Marco: We'll need SAML SSO, audit logs, key management — ideally HSM-backed KMS. Data residency constraints in EU for some customers.
02:14 Amira: OK good. Quick clarifying question: are you looking to fully replace OpenAI/Anthropic or have Redwood as a unified serving layer with fallbacks?
02:23 Jordan: We want parity first — if Redwood can serve the same model outputs (or at least deterministic-ish with fixed seeds) we could consolidate. But we might keep fallback to OpenAI for any gap during rollout.
02:36 Liam: On parity: we usually test with canonical prompt sets and measure metrics like intent accuracy, hallucination rate, token length distributions. Can you share a small eval set?
02:47 Priya: Yes we can share a 250-prompt eval harness — it's redacted for customer data. We'll include prompts that trip safety and edge-case contexts.
02:55 Sofia: Great, that helps. For compatibility we support standard tokenizers and common model formats; we also have sampling knobs that mirror temperature, top_p, top_k. Function-calling — depends on model variant but we support structured output + tool invocation patterns in our Hosted API.
03:12 Priya: Important — how do you handle KV cache and prefix caching? vLLM's KV behavior is a big part of our latency profile.
03:21 Liam: We expose continuous KV cache semantics and prefix caching; it's configurable per-route. We also do automatic batching but with latency SLOs so you can bias toward lower latency at cost of less batching.
03:36 Jordan: Autoscaling — when traffic spikes we need immediate burst capacity, our current vLLM autoscale takes minutes which is bad. Can Redwood burst across pool types?
03:47 Amira: Yes — in Dedicated customers can configure burst policies and we can route to hosted capacity as graceful fallback. For Private/VPC you can enable reserved pools and pre-warmed capacity; we'll walk through the config.
03:58 Marco: On encryption: at-rest, in-flight, and customer-managed keys?
04:04 Sofia: All supported. Hosted: we offer CMK via KMS integrations (AWS/GCP/Azure). Dedicated: customer KMS optional. Private: full HSM/KMS integration and audit logs retained per contract.
04:16 Marco: What's retention for audit logs? We sometimes need 7 years for certain regs.
04:21 Amira: We have enterprise add-ons for extended retention; we'll share the security pack with exact SLAs and retention options.
04:30 Leah: Cost — can you give rough delta between staying with OpenAI vs Redwood hosted vs Dedicated?
04:36 Amira: We'll share a TCO spreadsheet but high level: hosted is competitive with OpenAI on per-token but gives more observability; Dedicated lowers unit cost at commit levels but needs min commit; Private has higher fixed infra cost but gives isolation and potentially cheaper per token at scale.
04:54 Priya: Another technical question: tokenizer differences have bitten us — do you provide canonical tokenizer mapping or mashers to get 1:1 tokenization?
05:03 Liam: We include tokenizer parity tooling and can run tokenization diffs as part of the bench. Sometimes you need model-specific tokenizers; we onboard those and run compatibility jobs.
05:18 Jordan: About TGI — some of our models are served via TGI wrappers; will Redwood accept TGI artifacts or do we need to re-export?
05:28 Sofia: We accept TorchScript, ONNX, and a range of common formats. For TGI, often it's a thin wrapper; we'll work with your artifact and provide a quick adapter. There may be slight performance differences to test.
05:43 Priya: For eval parity how do you handle randomness seeds and temperature? We need repeatable comparisons.
05:50 Liam: We can lock RNG seeds, fix sampling to deterministic paths, and provide ledgered eval runs. We'll run A/B between your vLLM runs and Redwood's served model to surface deltas.
06:05 Jordan: Who owns the model versions? We need ability to pin specific versions and do canary rollouts.
06:12 Amira: You can pin model versions per-route, and we support canary rollouts and automatic fallback to previous model if error thresholds hit. Rollouts can be percentage-based or header-based.
06:25 Marco: SSO integration — do you support SCIM and SAML? We need role-based provisioning.
06:31 Sofia: Yes SAML, SCIM, RBAC controls, and per-token auditing.
06:36 Leah: On observability — we'd want token-level cost and tracing to tie errors back to prompts.
06:42 Liam: That's in Redwood Console: token breakdown, trace hooks, and per-route dashboards; we can demo that in the POC.
06:52 Jordan: Great. Any caveats around function-calling compatibility — our app relies on structured json outputs for function calls.
07:00 Liam: We support function calling with schema guidance; some older open models differ in emitted schema but we can map and validate. We'll include example adapters.
07:12 Priya: Bench plan — what's the POC look like? We want a week to run parity, 72-hour burst test, and security review.
07:20 Amira: Typical POC: 1) initial onboarding + small data/keys 2) run eval harness (you provide prompts) 3) run perf benchmarks including steady-state and burst 4) security review and KMS test 5) go/no-go. We usually run this 2–3 weeks but can compress to 1 week for focused parity and perf.
07:40 Jordan: Who does the benchmark infra? We prefer Redwood to run from your infra to see real behavior, but we'll provide traffic shaping and sample dataset.
07:50 Liam: We can run both: our quick internal bench and an on-customer run against Private/Dedicated to mirror your network. We'll give a benchmark spreadsheet so you can see tests and metrics.
08:04 Marco: Will you sign an NDA? We have customer data concerns.
08:09 Amira: Yes — we'll resend the NDA link and we have a standardized PII handling addendum.
08:15 Leah: Decision criteria: parity within X% on intent accuracy, median latency <200ms for 95% short-turn, cost per 1M tokens within N% of budget, and security sign-off.
08:30 Jordan: Also ease of rollback — if outputs diverge, we need quick fallback to current provider.
08:36 Sofia: Easy — multi-route routing policies can divert to OpenAI fallback with header-based overrides.
08:42 Priya: Any known gotchas from customers migrating away from Anthropic? We use some of Anthropic's safety features.
08:48 Liam: Safety wrappers differ; we'll help port safety prompts, and if you use Anthropic-specific features we'll map them to Redwood runtime policies or keep Anthropic as a step in pipeline during rollout. Some teams see small shifts in specific safety edge cases — that's why eval harness is vital.
09:05 Jordan: Will Redwood support running our TGI custom extensions? We maintain a few tokenizer tweaks and a custom sampling kernel.
09:13 Liam: We can onboard those, but low-level kernels may need recompilation. We'll work with your engineers; it might extend the POC timeline by a few days.
09:25 Marco: For Private deployment (on-prem) what network access does Redwood need? Are there open egress requirements?
09:32 Sofia: For on-prem package we can operate air-gapped; for VPC we need egress for control plane telemetry, or you can opt for a private control plane. We'll detail network ports in the security pack.
09:45 Amira: Quick note — many customers start with Dedicated so they get predictable performance without fully committing to on-prem. Dedicated also lets you bring CMKs.
09:57 Leah: Are there exit fees if we stop a Dedicated contract?
10:01 Amira: Terms vary — we'll include contract language and examples; usually there's a minimum commit term. We'll work with sales/legal to align with your procurement.
10:12 Jordan: Ok good. Can we run a small parity run — say 250 prompts — and a 6-hour burst test next week?
10:20 Amira: Yes, we can schedule that. Liam will own the bench run and Sofia will help onboard.
10:25 Liam: I'll prepare the bench plan and share the google sheet / benchmark spreadsheet link: https://redwood.app/bench/veridian (internal link).
10:33 Marco: Please include KMS integration points; we'll need to validate CMK rotation and HSM access.
10:40 Amira: We'll include a KMS playbook.
10:44 Leah: Ok, recap and next steps?
10:48 Amira: Quick recap: Redwood to share POC plan + TCO spreadsheet, security pack + NDA, bench spreadsheet. Veridian to share eval prompts and sample dataset and list of gating items. Schedule live bench for week of 2025-03-31 or 2025-04-07.
11:08 Jordan: Sounds good.
11:10 Amira: Any last questions?
11:12 Priya: One small ask — can we get a tokenization diff report before the bench? Helps us triage.
11:16 Liam: Yep I'll generate a tokenization diff run quickly after onboarding and include it in the bench doc.
11:22 Marco: We'll review the security pack and come back with specific redlines.
11:26 Amira: Great — thanks everyone, we'll follow up with links and the POC checklist.
11:31 Meeting end.
